newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Market seen favouring China-concept retail IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Market seen favouring China-concept retail IPOs.

text.p: Initial public offerings (IPOs) by China-concept retail stocks are expected to outperform their Hong Kong equivalents, analysts say.
While retail sales in Hong Kong have been sluggish, recent credit easing in China is expected to prompt a pick up in consumer spending there.

"There is the big story about China retail. It's a huge market - the potential for growth is explosive particularly as China emerges from hard economic times," said Keith Irving, head of research at HG Asia.

Analysts pointed to the success of casual wear maker and retailer Glorious Sun Enterprises Ltd's initial public offering in September. The retail portion of its offering was 236 times subscribed, the highest subscription rate this year.

Glorious Sun has a distribution network of 203 shops in China, mainly in provinces outside Guangdong, and 146 shops in Australia and New Zealand. Its shares were offered at HK$1.60 and are now trading around HK$3.55.

Among the upcoming retailing IPOs expected to benefit from China links is Wah Lee Resources Ltd, a Hong Kong-based distributor of video and audio products in China. The company is expected to seek a listing in November, analysts said.

"They (China-concept retailers) can achieve relatively stronger growth compared with those in Hong Kong," said Rebecca Ng, analyst at Tai Fook Securities. "We don't see any significant factors (before the end of 1996) which can lead to a recovery in the local retail sector," she added.

The China Daily newspaper said in July that retail sales of consumer goods were expected to rise 25 percent in 1996 to 2.53 trillion yuan (US$305 billion). Retail sales in the first half rose 21 percent from the same year-ago period to US$137 billion.
Louisa Sung, analyst at Sassoon Securities, said exposure to other emerging markets would also give retailing IPOs a boost.

"Hong Kong is a very mature market already for retail sales so if you have regional exposure -- it doesn't matter where as long as it's an emerging market -- I think definitely people would give a few more points for those retailers," she said.
However, most upcoming retail IPOs are focused on the local market, analysts said.

These include shoe maker Mirabell Footwear Ltd, electrical appliances supplier Alpha Appliances Ltd, Japanese sushi chain Genroku Sushi Co Ltd, jewellery retailer Luk Fook Holdings Co Ltd and cosmetic distributor Sa Sa Cosmetic.

"I don't expect the upcoming retail counters to be very well received in the market as local investors know what the retail market is like in Hong Kong," said Sunny Chan, research director from Seapower Research.
Analysts said individual fundamentals such as the nature and popularity of a company's products were expected to dictate the market's response.

"The response to upcoming listings will depend on various factors such as the brand they carry, the acceptancy of their products and their retail distribution network," said Mansion House's Ng. "Pricing is also a factor."
Ng of Tai Fook Securities said H-share issues in the retail sector will come under the same scrutiny as other H-shares, which have generally been disappointing performers.
"The H-share retailers will depend on management style and transparency, while positioning in the market is important for local retailers," she said.
China's Nanjing Central Emporium Stock is expected to become the first Chinese retailer to list overseas, aiming at a flotation in Hong Kong in 1997, newspaper reports say.
